key_insight: α-stable score-based generative models can match heavy-tailed extremes better than Brownian diffusion, with tail behavior governed by tail-index matching rather than global Wasserstein convergence alone.
engineering_relevance: For simulation and generative modeling of rare events, finance, climate, or other heavy-tailed systems, choosing a stable process with the right α can improve extreme-quantile fidelity.
method: Non-asymptotic p-Wasserstein convergence analysis for scale-preserving α-stable generative dynamics.
Decomposes error from early stopping, initialization, score approximation, and time discretization.
Compares stable vs Brownian dynamics on compactly supported and power-law targets, emphasizing tail asymptotics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence guarantees and asymptotic tail/quantile analysis rather than an empirical benchmark or dataset-based evaluation.
watch_item: Tail-index matching is crucial: if α does not match the target tail index, the model may still converge globally while failing to reproduce extreme tails accurately.
paper_title: From Global to Tail Convergence: Dynamics of $α$-Stable Score-Based Generative Models
